title: Standardize external model intake, pinning SLAs, and staged deprecation playbook
creator: Sofia Martinez
body:
Background:
Many enterprise customers and partners are requesting onboarding of third-party models or specific pinned versions of models for compliance and consistency. Current intake is ad-hoc: requests arrive via support, SEs, and account teams and are handled by different PMs and Eng liaisons. This causes long lead times, undocumented pinning decisions, inconsistent deprecation notices, and surprise regressions in quality or latency.

Objective:
Create a single operational playbook and intake flow that: (1) standardizes the information required to evaluate external model additions and version pin requests, (2) defines SLAs and guardrails for version pinning and rollback, (3) creates a staged deprecation runway with communication templates, and (4) integrates required eval gates (quality, perf, security, license) up-front so enterprise requests can be executed predictably.

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- Reduce median time from request -> catalog decision from current ~28d to <=10d.
- 90% of enterprise pin requests processed with documented eval results and rollout plan.
- Zero incidents caused by unvetted pinned model deployments in the quarter after rollout.

Scope / In-scope deliverables:
- Canonical intake form (Confluence + internal Slack form) listing required fields: customer, use case, expected qps, sample prompts, regulatory constraints, required model license info, desired pin window, SLA tier, and fallback model(s).
- Triage scoring rubric that weighs: security/compliance, latency/cost delta, quality delta (evals), business impact, and operational cost. Document thresholds for automatic approval, manual review, and rejection.
- Pinning SLA: define minimal supported pin window (e.g., 30 days), extension process, required rollback data retention, and cost-sharing expectations for extended pins.
- Eval gate checklist (automated where possible): regression tests on benchmark prompt suite, latency/throughput profiles on target infra, license and embargo checks, privacy/KMS review, and adversarial prompt checks.
- Staged deprecation policy: notice windows by customer tier (e.g., 60/30/14 days), mandatory migration plan, technical migration helpers (compatibility shim or alias routing), and customer-facing comms templates.
- Rollout & canary strategy for pinned models: small percentage traffic routing, monitoring dashboards for quality and latency regressions, and automatic fallback triggers.
- Integration points with Console: add fields for "pinned_by_customer" and pin metadata to model-catalog UI; surface pin expiration and migration notes.
- Operational runbook for escalations and when to refuse pins (e.g., unsupported license, security risk, >2x latency).

Non-goals:
- Not covering open-source upstream model governance (that is a separate legal/policy effort).
- Not implementing full automation for every eval gate in initial roll-out; some steps may be manual.

Risks:
- Increased operational overhead for long-term pinned versions (storage, model hosting cost).
- Legal/licensing complexities for some third-party models require legal sign-off and may stall decisions.
- Overly permissive pin windows could freeze progress on runtime optimizations.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Sofia Martinez (owner)
- Eng owners: Jacob O'Neil (catalog), Priya Shah (runtime), Marcus Lee (deploy)
- Legal: Anika Rao
- Security/Privacy: Omar Bennett
- Solutions/SE: Carla Gomez
- Customer Success: Ethan Brooks

Open questions (to resolve in kickoff):
1) What is the maximum allowed pin window without exec signoff? Proposed: 90 days.
2) Does Redwood charge an explicit premium for pinned-capacity in Dedicated? Proposed: yes, formula TBD.
3) What minimum eval suite must pass for auto-approval? Proposed: no regressions >5% on quality score and <=1.5x latency cost.

Proposed timeline / milestones:
- Week 0–2: Draft intake form + triage rubric; align with Legal and Security for required fields.
- Week 3–4: Build Confluence intake + Slack workflow; prototype catalog metadata fields for pins.
- Week 5–7: Implement eval checklist automation for quality + perf smoke tests; dashboard prototype for pinned models.
- Week 8: Internal beta with 2 enterprise customers; collect feedback.
- Week 10: Public rollout of playbook + console UI flags.

Next steps (this ticket):
- Kickoff with stakeholders (Sofia, Jacob, Priya, Legal, Security).
- Create Confluence draft and link to this ticket.
- Build initial triage rubric and simulation on historical requests to validate thresholds.
- Book 90-minute design/triage workshop with SEs and CS for March 2026 (owners: Sofia + Carla).
